Autonomous Logistics Robot SOTO for Your Production
Auto­mate your mate­r­ial flow and intral­o­gis­tics processes and close the gap between ware­house and production

Case studies
Flex­i­ble
Logis­tics robot SOTO can be flex­i­bly inte­grated into your pro­duc­tion envi­ron­ment: it can pick at dif­fer­ent heights, han­dle small load car­ri­ers (totes / KLTs) of dif­fer­ent sizes and inter­act with pas­sive flow racks. SOTO is able to trans­port up to 24 KLTs in one go and ulti­mately replaces your tug­ger train process com­pletely. With just a few clicks, you can adapt your tote deliv­ery processes your­self and always keep an eye on the entire mate­r­ial flow. As you grow, you can sim­ply and eas­ily inte­grate addi­tional SOTOs into your logis­tics chain.
Autonomous
Take repet­i­tive and phys­i­cally demand­ing trans­porta­tion tasks off your employ­ees’ hands. KLT robot SOTO trans­ports full and empty con­tain­ers pre­cisely to the right place 24/7 — autonomously and safely thanks to sophis­ti­cated sen­sor and cam­era tech­nol­ogy. This allows you to shift repet­i­tive, phys­i­cally demand­ing trans­porta­tion tasks to the robot and free up human resources for value-adding tasks. Auto­mated processes also help you to reduce incor­rect deliv­er­ies and make your processes more robust.
Intel­li­gent
SOTO is con­nected to your WMS sys­tem and uses its own intel­li­gence to plan the most effi­cient route for its trans­port orders, ensur­ing fast processes for your mate­r­ial flow. In addi­tion, SOTO reacts inde­pen­dently to changes in its envi­ron­ment, avoids obsta­cles and proac­tively rec­ti­fies disruptions.
Safe
SOTO puts safety first. The logis­tics robot is equipped with sev­eral laser scan­ners for safe nav­i­ga­tion, even in nar­row envi­ron­ments. It uses two 3D cam­eras to reli­ably detect obsta­cles such as machines and peo­ple. It always adapts its speed to its sur­round­ings so that it can always avoid  obsta­cles or stop in time. Light cur­tains also pre­vent peo­ple from inter­fer­ing with the run­ning system.

Auto­mate your mate­r­ial flow and close the gap between ware­house and pro­duc­tion line
Flexibility
The autonomous logistics robot SOTO closes the gap between warehouse and production. It transports up to 24 totes of different sizes simultaneously and interacts with a wide variety of transfer stations at different heights. It can approach sources and sinks from three sides and rotate KLTs as required after picking them up. This allows you to keep the material flow running at all times, supply all stations just in time and relieve your employees of these 'unproductive' tasks.
100%
End-to-end autom­a­ti­za­tion
Process Stability
By automating your KLT transports, you can now ensure smooth, precise and safe processing of your transport orders - without having to struggle with the challenges of vacation periods, sickness waves or shift work. We base our SOTO on the highest industry standards so that you can optimize your transport processes and raise them to a new level of reliability.
> 98%
Sys­tem availability
Efficiency
Reduce your ongoing intralogistics costs by an average of 60% through intelligent automation of transport processes. SOTO handles totes for you safely and reliably around the clock - regardless of whether you are loading all stations for the day shift during the night shift or whether you want to cushion production peaks.
60%
Cost sav­ings
Autonomous logis­tics robot SOTO in action
Dynamic sup­ply and dis­posal of small load carriers
The logis­tics robot SOTO has already suc­cess­fully taken over the sup­ply of mate­ri­als via KLTs in a wide range of indus­tries and for both large and medium-sized com­pa­nies.
With its high level of intel­li­gence, SOTO is able to per­form com­plex trans­porta­tion tasks inde­pen­dently and react smoothly to changes in the envi­ron­ment.
It can there­fore com­pletely replace man­ual intral­o­gis­tics processes for you.

Max­i­mum flex­i­bil­ity at han­dover stations
SOTO uses a con­veyor grip­per to manip­u­late KLTs at vari­able heights between 0.40 — 1.70 m. This ensures the robot can inter­act with a wide range of han­dover sta­tions, such as the following:
Flow racks
SOTO picks-up and places KLTs into the com­part­ments of flow racks. All com­mon rack types can be adapted with lit­tle effort so that SOTO can inter­act with them.
Con­veyor belts
The mobile robot can be eas­ily con­fig­ured via the fleet man­ager to inter­act with sta­tion­ary con­vey­ors con­nected to an AS/RS or a machine.
Tug­ger trains
SOTO trans­fers or removes KLTs at the exact posi­tion on a tug­ger train if this is of advan­tage for your processes.
Tech­nol­ogy & Safety
SOTO deliv­ers a con­sis­tent and highly adapt­able mate­r­ial flow between the ware­house and the pro­duc­tion line. Thanks to its pow­er­ful Li-ion bat­ter­ies, it can drive for up to 8 hours with­out recharg­ing. The bat­ter­ies can be recharged at any time to max­i­mize effi­ciency (charg­ing ratio: 1 minute charg­ing = 5 min­utes driving).
The mobile KLT robot inte­grates high-end tech­nol­ogy into every com­po­nent. The sen­sors and intel­li­gent soft­ware enable pin­point-accu­rate han­dling of con­tain­ers, and safe nav­i­ga­tion in mixed envi­ron­ments with human colleagues.

The omni­di­rec­tional power drive enables SOTO to maneu­ver pre­cisely, even in the nar­row­est spaces. Aisle widths as nar­row as 1.65m are fully nav­i­ga­ble; from 2.5m wide aisles, SOTO can achieve its max­i­mum speed of 1.5m/s. The drive base is extremely robust and meets the high­est safety demands through its high brak­ing performance.
SOTO is a ‘multi-load robot.’ With its dou­ble-deep back­pack for stor­ing con­tain­ers, SOTO can trans­port between 8 and 24 totes simul­ta­ne­ously. The back­pack con­fig­u­ra­tion depends on the range of KLT sizes and your trans­port require­ments. The high trans­port vol­ume allows you to sig­nif­i­cantly reduce the vol­ume of traf­fic in your production.
Indi­vid­ual totes  can weigh up to 20kg, with the robot hav­ing a total pay­load capac­ity of 250kg. The robot can reli­ably pick and place KLTs rang­ing in size from 300x200 mm to 600x400mm.
SOTO uses a flex­i­ble grip­per mech­a­nism to trans­fer KLTs between heights of 0.4m and 1.7m from the ground. For effi­cient stor­age, SOTO can also rotate KLTs by 90° and 180° degrees, for exam­ple, to pick them up length­wise and drop them off width­wise. The grip­per can pick up and place con­tain­ers from three direc­tions: left, right, and front.
Bar­code scan­ners on the grip­per ensure that the cor­rect tote is picked up and placed in the right loca­tion. This enables mate­r­ial track­ing in the fleet man­ager at all times. Thanks to its sen­sors, cam­eras, and intel­li­gent soft­ware, SOTO is also capa­ble of react­ing to changes in its envi­ron­ment dur­ing oper­a­tion, such as a shifted shelf or incor­rectly labeled KLT.
Laser scan­ners at the front and rear, as well as 3D cam­eras, ensure safe nav­i­ga­tion in dynamic envi­ron­ments. The robot rec­og­nizes obsta­cles while dri­ving, adjusts its speed, and uses the per­mit­ted space to nav­i­gate around them. Light cur­tains around the grip­per ensure that humans do not come into con­tact with mov­ing parts. If a light cur­tain detects an object, the robot imme­di­ately stops all movements.
If SOTO encoun­ters a prob­lem that requires human assis­tance, the touch dis­play shows rel­e­vant infor­ma­tion to quickly rec­tify the prob­lem. This means that even col­leagues with no prior knowl­edge of robot­ics can see where the prob­lem lies and eas­ily fix it.

SOTO Fleet Man­ager — VDA5050-com­pli­ant con­trol soft­ware for your SOTO fleet
In con­trast to sim­ple robot­ics solu­tions on the mar­ket, SOTO is an autonomous, per­cep­tion-con­trolled robot. The “brain” of SOTO, takes con­trol of the com­plex nav­i­ga­tion, safety and logis­tics tasks and brings them together in the SOTO Fleet Man­ager. This intel­li­gent soft­ware also
enables SOTO to solve chal­lenges inde­pen­dently
.
You will quickly find your way around the min­i­mal­ist user inter­face.
Here you can record new pro­duc­tion envi­ron­ments and put SOTO into oper­a­tion
, with­out hav­ing to wait for exter­nal support.
The SOTO Fleet Man­ager is con­nected to your WMS sys­tem via an inter­face. This means that you not only have your SOTO fleet in view at all times, but also every trans­port order and the entire mate­r­ial flow.
The KLT robot SOTO is
VDA5050-com­pli­ant
and can also be con­nected to a 3rd party mas­ter con­troller if you are oper­at­ing a mixed fleet of robots from sev­eral ven­dors. Our team is happy to advise you on your exact requirements.
Mapping & Modeling
Using its sensors, SOTO records its surroundings and creates a map for localization. In the fleet manager, this map is supplemented with all relevant information, including sources, sinks, routes, and traffic rules. You can make adjustments at any time to accommodate changes to your production environment.
Operation & Control
The fleet manager provides a live view of all robots to keep track of their location, transported materials and future tasks. You can view all the relevant KPIs directly on a centralized dashboard.
Order Management & Route Planning
The fleet manager also provides an overview of all active and pending orders. The master controller ensures an optimal distribution across the fleet to guarantee a fast process.

Smart logistics with the commissioning robot TORU
Auto­mate the stor­age and retrieval of shoe boxes or cus­tom KLTs from shelv­ing racks.
Inte­gra­tion
Transfer systems
Technology & Safety
Fleet Management
TORU
Inte­gra­tion
Com­mis­sion­ing robot TORU inte­grates eas­ily and with­out major adjust­ments into an exist­ing ware­house and processes. Once con­fig­ured, it works autonomously along­side its human col­leagues. The con­nec­tion to a ware­house man­age­ment sys­tem is uncom­pli­cated via WLAN.
Oper­a­tion
Shoe boxes are its spe­cialty: the intel­li­gent pick­ing robot TORU picks indi­vid­ual boxes — even from stacks — and takes them directly to the trans­fer sta­tion. Of course, it also brings them back again for stor­age or returns. Up to 20 hours a day. This allows him to be active out­side reg­u­lar work shifts and, for exam­ple, smooth out peaks through prepara­tory work. After an update, TORU also picks up spe­cial small load car­ri­ers (KLTs) as an inte­gral part of the NEOin­tral­o­gis­tics logis­tics sys­tem in its proven reli­able manner.
Scal­ing
Pick­ing with TORU not only adapts to your ware­house envi­ron­ment, but also to your needs: New robots can be inte­grated directly, as they inherit their knowl­edge from the TORU(s) already imple­mented. Your robot fleet grows with your success.

Pick­ing robot TORU in action
The mobile pick­ing robot TORU is ideal for sort­ing orders into ded­i­cated com­part­ments and pick­ing up boxes for the stor­age process. It picks indi­vid­ual shoe­boxes or spe­cial
NEO-KLTs
and trans­ports them to a trans­fer point. Here, TORU can con­sol­i­date dif­fer­ent items in a sin­gle order so that the pack­ag­ing process can be ini­ti­ated directly.

Flex­i­bil­ity for your processes: Trans­fer sta­tions at a glance
TORU inte­grates per­fectly into your cur­rent processes. No mat­ter which trans­fer sta­tions you use in your ware­house or pick­ing process. TORU reli­ably han­dles the great­est pos­si­ble vari­ance within an oper­at­ing range of 8 cm to 250 cm above the floor:
Con­veyor belt
Picked car­tons can be placed directly on con­veyor sticks to be fed to a sorter, for exam­ple, or to the auto­matic pack­ing line.
Flow rack
TORU places car­tons directly into flow racks and picks from them. The han­dling is suit­able for down­stream tote processes as well as sin­gle & multi orders.
Order pick­ing trolley
Shoe boxes can be picked up from or deliv­ered to pick­ing trol­leys. Ideal for sort­ing orders and other inbound & out­bound processes.
Put­wall
Pick­ing via the put­wall syn­chro­nises pick-by-light com­part­ment dis­plays and thus offers max­i­mum flex­i­bil­ity in sort­ing orders and sub­se­quent processes.
Tech­nol­ogy & safety: Com­mis­sion­ing robot TORU in detail
The pick­ing robot TORU helps your human col­leagues to han­dle order pick­ing with sig­nif­i­cantly less effort. It works just about 24/7 and gives you greater inde­pen­dence from order peaks and staff plan­ning dur­ing off-peak shifts, vaca­tion peri­ods or sick­ness waves.
TORU com­bines high-end tech­nol­ogy with intel­li­gent soft­ware and the high­est safety stan­dards for safe work­ing side by side with people.

Due to the autonomous nav­i­ga­tion of the robot, no adjust­ments by the cus­tomer in the form of lines or bar­codes on the floor are necessary.
The lift­ing col­umn enables fast, pre­cise posi­tion­ing of the grip­per to any grip­ping height as well as agile rota­tion between the stor­age rack and the backpack.
The grip­per trav­els in the lift­ing col­umn and grabs boxes or stacks from the rack with its pow­er­ful suc­tion unit.
In its inte­grated back­pack rack, TORU trans­ports car­tons that have already been picked to the trans­fer sta­tion or objects to be stored to the stor­age zone.

Fleet Man­age­ment for your TORU Fleet
With ARC (Advanced Robot Con­trol), users always have an overview of the entire fleet, the indi­vid­ual TORU-robot as well as the order man­age­ment and rel­e­vant KPIs:
Con­trol of the robot fleet
ARC is the con­trol cen­ter of the TORU fleet and is con­nected to the inven­tory man­age­ment sys­tem. On a day-to-day basis, ARC not only offers full trans­parency of all robots, order manage­ment and KPIs, but also pro­vides instruc­tions on how to solve problems.
Visual Rep­re­sen­ta­tion
The visual map dis­play in your own ware­house makes con­trol­ling the fleet par­tic­u­larly intu­itive. It shows where the indi­vid­ual robots are on the move in the ware­house, which orders they are pro­cessing, which items they are cur­r­ent­ly trans­port­ing and which actions are com­ing up next.
Track­ing  of KPIs
Rel­e­vant KPIs are recorded in real time and clearly dis­played. The data overview offers full trans­parency at all times. For exam­ple, fleet per­for­mance over a period of time, aver­age uti­liza­tion or the cur­rent sta­tus of the trans­fer stations.
Order Man­age­ment
Order man­age­ment ensures opti­mal struc­tur­ing of trans­port orders to guar­an­tee a fast process. Cur­rent orders are dis­trib­uted in the fleet and can be read at any time.
Human Process Coordination
ARC also coor­di­nates the processes between robots and humans. Employ­ees can see directly which pick­ing trol­ley is ready for pick-up.
Remote Oper­a­tions
The remote oper­a­tions team mon­i­tors robot activ­i­ties 24 hours a day, 6 days a week, and can proac­tively assist remotely if needed, increas­ing fleet availability.
Autonomous stor­age and retrieval of shoe boxes or spe­cial KLTs in shelf­ing racks.
Piece-pre­cise order picking
Tar­geted grip­ping and stack­ing of boxes
TORU has a pre­cise vac­uum grip­per arm. This allows it to pick up, lift and place car­tons or spe­cial totes weigh­ing up to 5.8 kg, with a max. size of 390 x 280 x 145 mm (L x W x H), with piece-by-piece pre­ci­sion. Even entire stacks if necessary.
Autonomous per­cep­tion
2D and 3D cameras
TORU locates objects to be picked and free stor­age loca­tions on the shelf. Using intel­li­gent algo­rithms, TORU searches for the bar­codes and can thus iden­tify the cor­rect object.
High trans­port capacity
16 boxes and a wide range of action
TORU can trans­port up to 16 objects simul­ta­ne­ously in its back­pack rack. With its action range of 8 cm to 250 cm above the ground, it even sur­passes human agility — with­out any back pain.
Safety is always the top priority for TORU
Our robots are safe when dealing with people. To this end, we have equipped them with a state-of-the-art person recognition system from certified manufacturers. We also work closely with the occupational safety specialists in our customers’ factories on site to ensure smooth integration.
